findingApprovals.fpLevel.allHelp: Every false positive needs a second person to approve it.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.description: When marking a finding a false positive needs a second person. An accepted risk always needs a second person, whatever you choose here.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.high_and_aboveH: A second person approves a false positive on a critical or high finding, a known exploited vulnerability (KEV), P0 or P1, a validated exploit, or a crown-jewel or internet-exposed asset. Anyone with approval permission may decide the others alone.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.lowerDelay: A lower level takes effect 24 hours after you save it, and every approver is told. A higher level takes effect at once.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.lowerPercentDel: A lower second-look share takes effect 24 hours after you save it. A higher share takes effect at once.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.offHelp: Anyone with approval permission may mark any finding a false positive alone.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.offWarning: A single stolen session or a single mistake can mark a critical finding a false positive. Decisions stay audited and get a review flag when the finding later changes, but nobody checks them first.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.offWarningTitle: One person can hide any finding
findingApprovals.fpLevel.pendingBody: "{level}" takes effect at {at}. Until then "{current}" applies.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.pendingPercentB: {next} % takes effect at {at}. Until then {current} % of single-person decisions get a second look.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.pendingPercentT: A lower second-look share is waiting
findingApprovals.fpLevel.secondLookHelp: A random share of false positives decided by one person is flagged for another person to look at. 0 turns it off; at most 10.
findingApprovals.fpLevel.title: False-positive approval
findingApprovals.selfApprove.audited: It is recorded in the audit log and marked self-approved everywhere.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.badgeTitle: Approved by its own requester, the organization's only member
findingApprovals.selfApprove.description: Nobody else in your organization can decide this request. As its only member and owner you may approve it yourself.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.doneShorten: Approved. The acceptance was shortened to the limit for a self-approval.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.error.badCo: The code is wrong or was already used. Wait for a new code and try again.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.error.needs: Turn on two-factor authentication first: approving your own request needs a code from your authenticator app.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.error.notAl: You can approve your own request only as the owner of an organization with no other active member.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.limit: An accepted risk ends within 7 days (P0 or known exploited), 45 days (P1) or 90 days.
findingApprovals.selfApprove.reasonLabel: Why may it take effect without a second person?
findingApprovals.selfApprove.title: Approve your own request
findingApprovals.selfApprove.told: Your organization's notification channels and its backup contact are told.
findingApprovals.settings.backupDescript: An advisor or auditor outside the organization who is emailed whenever its only member approves their own finding request.
findingApprovals.settings.cancelFailed: Could not cancel the waiting change
findingApprovals.settings.savedPending: Saved. The lower level takes effect in 24 hours; the approvers were told.
findingApprovals.single.applied: Marked a false positive. It is recorded with your name and reason.
findingApprovals.single.badgeTitle: Decided by one person: the organization's false-positive level did not require a second
findingApprovals.single.notice: This organization doesn't require approval for this finding: it is marked a false positive at once. Choose a reason and explain it; the decision is audited and flagged for review if the finding later becomes more serious.
findingApprovals.single.othersNotice: A person with approval permission could mark this finding a false positive alone; your request waits for one of them.
